title: Disable system sleep on the DGX Spark
head: f8aa8fd9230a
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The sleep-disabled helper tests a file's existence, not effective systemd sleep policy
leads.consequence: On a Spark with an empty or malformed existing omarchy-dgx-spark.conf, or a lexically later drop-in re-enabling sleep, the helper still returns true. Suspend and Hibernate disappear from Omarchy's menu, the toggle reports sleep disabled, hibernation setup refuses, although systemd does not have the corresponding disabled policy. With an existing empty file the migration exits 0 and bin/omarchy-migrate:93-95 records permanent completion instead of repairing it. The helper has no error feedback and each subsequent migration invocation skips after the marker is set. Compare parsed Allow* settings or treat an existing but invalid/ineffective file as repairable; add empty-file and override fixtures.
leads.triage: dropped: contrived, Omarchy writes the full file

leads.summary: Following the manual's remove-the-file opt-out is undone by a supported hardware reapply
leads.consequence: Removing the drop-in makes the helper false, then running the documented rerunnable omarchy-apply-hardware on the same Spark recreates the four no switches and hides the menu again. This is not a package update or ordinary login: it requires a hardware reapply, a supported diagnostic/install workflow. No marker preserves the administrator's decision and no warning explains the new disablement. Make the opt-out persistent or document that reapplying hardware will undo it, and test the lifecycle.
leads.triage: confirmed factual by coordinator (bin/omarchy-apply-hardware:16-18,75) and Sol sandbox rerun of the install script; also in Opus hypotheses; published as optional note

leads.summary: A missing DMI field silently completes the one-shot migration without applying the Spark policy
leads.consequence: Linux creates sys_vendor and product_name sysfs attributes only when their DMI values are reported. If either is unavailable at the update where the migration runs, detector failure is treated as 'not a Spark': script exits 0 and the per-user migration marker is written even though no drop-in exists. A later DMI fix or firmware update does not rerun it; an affected Spark keeps system sleep enabled unless an administrator explicitly reapplies hardware setup. This is a conditional kernel/input edge case, not an assertion that actual DGX Spark firmware omits DMI. Distinguish inaccessible/missing identification from a definite nonmatch before treating a machine-wide safety migration as complete.
leads.triage: dropped: speculative, no evidence a Spark lacks the fields

leads.summary: Removing the Omarchy package leaves its machine-wide sleep ban in place
leads.consequence: The installer writes /etc/systemd/sleep.conf.d/omarchy-dgx-spark.conf but the package recipe ships only source bin/install/migration files, not that generated /etc file, and specifies no package-removal hook. Removing Omarchy by package manager therefore removes its helper and menu but does not remove the machine-wide systemd sleep policy. The system still refuses suspend/hibernation until the administrator manually deletes the drop-in; this is especially easy to miss when switching distributions. Add explicit uninstall guidance or a safe cleanup route; do not remove it during a normal package update.

leads.summary: The DGX test passes with the new hibernation setup guard deleted in an isolated environment
leads.consequence: In the project's command-only test sandbox /sys/power/image_size is absent. hibernation-setup:16-19 exits before it reaches the new guard; the test only checks for the guard's message when that sysfs file exists. An actual mutant with lines 21-24 deleted passed the full DGX test with exit 0, so this test does not protect the newly added guard in CI environments without hibernation support. Use an injectable private image_size path or a safe isolated fake kernel sysfs fixture, and assert the expected message and absence of swap actions unconditionally; never run the unguarded real hibernation branch against /etc.

limits: No DGX Spark hardware or NVIDIA DGX OS image was supplied; no claim is made about observed firmware DMI availability or DGX OS's exact shipped sleep config.

The head's focused DGX, bin-style, menu and menu-guards tests and CLI commands --check all passed in a verified review.py sandbox at LC_ALL=C. No systemd daemon, hardware, host logind, full test/cli suite, or graphical compositor was executed.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `f8aa8fd`, the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13260#issuecomment-5854462845)'s finding is resolved; one small test gap remains.

- Menu rows, suspend toggle, hibernation setup and manual: **resolved**.
- The four earlier test regressions: **resolved**, each fails the test now.
- #12826 still edits the same Suspend line.

### The hibernation-setup test check depends on the machine

Without `/sys/power/image_size` (an empty `/sys`, or no kernel hibernation support), `omarchy-hibernation-setup` exits before the new `omarchy-sleep-disabled` check, and the test compares the message only when that file exists. **Impact:** there, deleting the new check still passes.

**Suggested change:** Move the `omarchy-sleep-disabled` block above the `/sys/power/image_size` check and drop the test's `if [[ -f /sys/power/image_size ]]` wrapper.

<details><summary>Reproducer (passes at f8aa8fd with the new check deleted, without /sys/power/image_size)</summary>

Commit: f8aa8fd9230a5caae139ca3a69b089496e234eb0. Run from the repository root on a machine where `/sys/power/image_size` does not exist (a container or sandbox with an empty `/sys`, or a kernel without hibernation support).

1. Remove the new refusal from `bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup` and run the PR's test unchanged:

```bash
sed -i '/^if omarchy-sleep-disabled; then$/,/^fi$/d' bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup
bash test/shell.d/dgx-spark-hardware-test.sh; echo "exit=$?"
```

Diff produced by the `sed`:

```diff
@@ -18,10 +18,6 @@
   exit 0
 fi
 
-if omarchy-sleep-disabled; then
-  echo "Hibernation is turned off on this machine" >&2
-  exit 0
-fi
 
 # When --no-rebuild is set, the caller is responsible for the UKI rebuild
```

Actual output (exit status 0):

```text
ok - the DGX Spark sleep setting runs at install and through a migration
ok - the detector matches only the DGX Spark
ok - the DGX Spark setting disallows every sleep operation and leaves other machines alone
ok - omarchy-sleep-disabled follows the sleep setting
ok - the migration applies the setting once, only on a Spark
ok - the suspend toggle and hibernation setup respect the disabled setting
ok - the menu hides Suspend and Hibernate only while sleep is disabled
```

The script stops at its `/sys/power/image_size` check (line 16) before it reaches the refusal, and the test only compares the message inside `if [[ -f /sys/power/image_size ]]` (lines 101-105).

2. Test case that does not depend on the machine: replace lines 101-105 of the test with an unconditional message check.

```diff
 hibernation=$(run spark "$scratch/spark" bash "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup" 2>&1) ||
   fail "hibernation setup exits cleanly while sleep is disabled"
-# Without kernel hibernation support the script stops earlier, before this check.
-if [[ -f /sys/power/image_size ]]; then
-  [[ $hibernation == *"Hibernation is turned off on this machine"* ]] ||
-    fail "hibernation setup says hibernation is turned off" "$hibernation"
-fi
+[[ $hibernation == *"Hibernation is turned off on this machine"* ]] ||
+  fail "hibernation setup says hibernation is turned off" "$hibernation"
```

At f8aa8fd9 (unmodified `bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup`), without `/sys/power/image_size`, actual output (exit status 1):

```text
ok - the DGX Spark sleep setting runs at install and through a migration
ok - the detector matches only the DGX Spark
ok - the DGX Spark setting disallows every sleep operation and leaves other machines alone
ok - omarchy-sleep-disabled follows the sleep setting
ok - the migration applies the setting once, only on a Spark
Hibernation is not supported on your system
not ok - hibernation setup says hibernation is turned off
```

With the `omarchy-sleep-disabled` block moved above the `/sys/power/image_size` check in `bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup`:

```diff
-if [[ ! -f /sys/power/image_size ]]; then
-  echo -e "Hibernation is not supported on your system" >&2
+if omarchy-sleep-disabled; then
+  echo "Hibernation is turned off on this machine" >&2
   exit 0
 fi
 
-if omarchy-sleep-disabled; then
-  echo "Hibernation is turned off on this machine" >&2
+if [[ ! -f /sys/power/image_size ]]; then
+  echo -e "Hibernation is not supported on your system" >&2
   exit 0
 fi
```

the same test passes (exit status 0, all seven `ok` lines), and with the block deleted instead it fails with `not ok - hibernation setup says hibernation is turned off` (exit status 1). With `/sys/power/image_size` present, the unmodified head and the moved-check version both pass the changed test.

Not executed (source reading only): on a machine that does have `/sys/power/image_size`, a missing or misplaced refusal is caught, but only after `bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup` has run past it with the test's `sudo` stub, which runs its arguments (`exec "$@"`, test lines 40-45). From line 67 on, the script reads the machine's `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_resume.conf` (if hibernation is already set up there, it stops with "Hibernation is already set up" and writes nothing). Otherwise it continues: the `gum confirm` stub succeeds, it reads `/etc/fstab`, and when that has no `/swap/swapfile` line, `sudo cp`/`sudo tee` target `/etc/fstab` (lines 108-111). `sudo /usr/bin/mktemp`/`install`/`mv` target `/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep` (lines 38-54, 123-127). For a normal user these writes are refused and the script exits 1 at line 126. Run as root they would succeed, and later steps would write `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_resume.conf`.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandbox, stubbed commands, private sleep-config and DMI paths):

- Menu guards (production guard script; drop-in × suspend toggled off × hibernation available): without the drop-in, all 4 combinations match `dragon`; with it, Suspend and Hibernate are hidden in all 4.
- `omarchy toggle suspend` with the drop-in leaves the flag unchanged and notifies "Suspend is turned off on this machine"; without it, it behaves as on `dragon`.
- `omarchy hibernation setup` with the drop-in and a simulated `/sys/power/image_size` prints "Hibernation is turned off on this machine", exits 0 and runs no swap or boot commands.
- Migration: one `sudo` call on a Spark without the drop-in, none with it or on other machines; a failing `sudo` exits 1.
- The updated test passes at `f8aa8fd`. `menu-test.sh`, `menu-guards-test.sh`, `bin-style-test.sh` and `test/cli` pass on head and `dragon`.

**Optional notes:**

1. The Hibernate row's `omarchy-hibernation-available` condition is untested: changing that `when` to `! omarchy-sleep-disabled` alone passes the PR's test, and no other test covers the Hibernate row, yet would show Hibernate on every machine without the drop-in. One more guard evaluation with the availability stub failing (as the suspend-off case already does) would catch it.
2. `omarchy apply hardware` (run as root) reruns `install/hardware/nvidia-dgx-spark.sh`, which rewrites the drop-in after a user has removed it (source, plus a sandbox rerun of that script), and removing it needs `sudo`. One sentence in the manual would cover both.
3. With the migration deleted, the test exits 1 without a `not ok` line, because the `grep -l … | head -1` substitution aborts under `set -euo pipefail` before the readable `fail`. Adding `|| true` inside the substitution should restore the message (not run).

**Hardware:** the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13260#issuecomment-5856481501) reports the detector matching and logind reporting all four `Can*` values as `no` on the Spark. The running menu was not checked by the author or here.
</details>
